title: legacy relay-roles advice must treat a directory the same way init does
lead: `store.legacy_roles_advice` tests the leftover `.slicer/relay-roles.md` with `exists()`, while `roles_init` tests it with `is_file()`. Both should use `is_file()`, so `check` never suggests a command that then refuses.
findings_note: s257 gate, 2026-10-13: store.legacy_roles_advice uses exists() while roles_init uses is_file(); a directory at .slicer/relay-roles.md gets advice that init --replace-legacy refuses
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any other legacy-file handling, and changing roles_init.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The s257 gate found that a directory at `.slicer/relay-roles.md` makes `check` warn "run `relay-roles init --replace-legacy`". That command then refuses, because the path is not a file. The warning should match what the command does.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - With a directory at `.slicer/relay-roles.md`, `check` gives no `legacy_relay_roles` warning, and `ai relay` gives no stderr warning.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Use `is_file()` in `legacy_roles_advice`.
2. Add the test and a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` Fixed entry.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- The full suite passes on Python 3.11+.
- `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s261`, branch `feature/s261-legacy-roles-isfile`. Commit only on the branch. Merging and pushing wait for the owner.
